## Personality

Eliza Andrews is characterized by a deeply ingrained pessimistic outlook. Her pervasive negativity is notable enough to serve as a point of comparison for others.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P60](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0060), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P24](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0024), [v2 XVII A Chapter of Accidents P64](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0064)_

## History

Eliza Andrews lived with her sister Catherine in a little brown house situated in a sunny corner of Mark Andrew's beech woods. When [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana Barry](../character/di.md) canvassed the neighborhood to collect subscriptions for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society), the pessimistic Eliza flatly refused to contribute any money to the cause. However, her sister Catherine secretly provided a donation behind her back shortly after Eliza declined.

_Sources: [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P6](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0006), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P8](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0008), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P11](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0011), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P13](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0013), [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P14](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0014), +62 more_

## Quotes

> "I don’t see the necessity. We didn’t gad about to halls and places when we were young, Catherine Andrews. This world is getting worse every day."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P18](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0018)

> "Doctors always talk like that just to keep people cheered up. I wouldn’t have much hope if I was her. It’s best to be prepared for the worst."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P27](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0027)

> “You think!” Miss Eliza’s voice expressed the utmost contempt. “It doesn’t signify what you think, Catherine Andrews. Facts is facts.”
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P20](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0020)

> "There isn’t any bright side."
>
> — Eliza Andrews — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P22](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0022)
